blocks.html: Short answer: Si Racha is a seaside town with a large Japanese community. For sea views and strolling stay by the seafront / Koh Loi; for Japanese restaurants, onsen and malls choose the J-Park (Japan town) area; and to catch boats to Koh Sichang, stay near the Koh Loi pier.

faq.q: Where is best to stay in Si Racha?
faq.a: For sea views and strolling, base by the seafront around Koh Loi and Surasak Montri Park, within walking distance of the pier and malls; if you love Japanese food and onsen, choose the J-Park area. Both are in the same town, a short ride apart.

faq.q: Why does Si Racha have so much Japanese influence?
faq.a: Si Racha sits near Laem Chabang Port and industrial estates with many Japanese companies, so a large Japanese community lives here, which has brought Japanese restaurants, supermarkets and Japanese-style community malls such as J-Park Nihon Mura — great if you like a Japanese atmosphere.

faq.q: How do I get to Koh Sichang from Si Racha?
faq.a: Take a boat from the Koh Loi pier in central Si Racha — about 45 minutes, with departures through the day. Staying near the pier makes it easier to catch a morning boat, good for a Koh Sichang day trip or an overnight on the island.
